precepts.text: Blow the trumpet, sanctify a fast, gather the children and the sucklings, and let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, no more weddings, while the priests weep and say spare thy people, because our people are dying; then the Lord is jealous for his land, and removes far off the northern army into the land of Israel between the Dead Sea and the Mediterranean, where his stink comes up.
precepts.point: An altar to the Lord in the midst of Egypt, and an altar is for sacrifice, the Israelites; they cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors, and he sends them a saviour and a great one, Christ, who delivers them, the same as Jeremiah 30:7.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “they shall cry unto the Lord because of the oppressors.” What will the oppressors be doing? The same thing 2 Esdras 16, Revelation 12:17, Matthew 10 and Matthew 24 say: Jacob's trouble. Joel shows the crying.

“Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly: Gather the people, sanctify the congregation, assemble the elders, gather the children, and those that suck the breasts.” This is going to be a major fast, because there will be so much devastation to our people. “Let the bridegroom go forth of his chamber, and the bride out of her closet”: when this fast goes out, we are not doing weddings or planning weddings. Weddings are finished. We have to pray to the Lord because our people are dying.

“Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord.” That is the cry of Isaiah 19, crying bitterly because there is going to be death. “And give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He answers, “I will send you corn, and wine, and oil” and “I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen: But I will remove far off from you the northern army.” That is the great multitude after us in 2 Esdras 16. He will “drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea.” The east sea is the Dead Sea and the utmost sea is the Mediterranean: the land of Israel between them, what they call the Middle East. The Lord is going to cause things to pop off there.

“And his stink shall come up, and his ill savour shall come up, because he hath done great things.” The Lord is going to destroy them over there: tribulation, World War III, Armageddon. It is all laid out for us. Yes, you are dying, but you are not dead; the Lord takes the northern army down, and then he sends us “a saviour, and a great one”, Christ, to deliver us.

precepts.text: The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, war and devastation, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come. Amos 5:18: woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord; it is darkness and not light, not the party you imagine. Zephaniah 1:14-15: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly; that day is a day of wrath, trouble, and distress. Matthew 24:29-30: after the tribulation the stars, missiles, fall from heaven, the powers of the nations are shaken with war, and all the tribes of the earth mourn when they see the Son of man coming. We will be running and weeping, not stomping and clapping.
precepts.point: This thou knowest, that all they which are in Asia be turned away from me, of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes: men who warred with Paul left the faith. We have seen a lot come and a lot go, so do not get too attached; you are strong today, we will see about tomorrow when affliction, tribulation, and persecution come. The Lord give mercy unto the house of Onesiphorus, who oft refreshed me, was not ashamed of my chain, and in Rome sought me out very diligently on foot, and ministered unto me at Ephesus; may he find mercy of the Lord in that day.

note.label: War & the Pain of Repentance

precepts.why:
“That day” in Paul’s words to Timothy is the second coming, and Joel shows what kind of day it is: “The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and the terrible day of the Lord come.” This is a time of war and devastation. When Christ returns, it is going to be a great and terrible day.

Amos says the same: “Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord! to what end is it for you? the day of the Lord is darkness, and not light.” We say we can’t wait for the day of the Lord because we don’t really comprehend the magnitude of what is going to happen. You think it is going to be a bright day and Christ will take us all up to the kingdom. It is not that type of a day; it is not that type of a party.

Zephaniah: “The great day of the Lord is near, it is near, and hasteth greatly, even the voice of the day of the Lord: the mighty man shall cry there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of trouble and distress.” Don’t think that when the Lord returns we are all going to be standing and cheering. We are going to be running and weeping.

Christ said it in Matthew 24: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days”, which is Jacob’s trouble, “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, because the sky will be black, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles dropping from the sky. The powers of the nations shall be shaken with war. “and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” You think you will be happy, stomping your feet and clapping; the Bible says all the tribes shall mourn, meaning cry bitterly. That is the day Paul was preparing Timothy for, and why he told him to stir up the gift, not fear, and not be ashamed of the afflictions of the gospel.

precepts.text: Deliverance is in Mount Zion and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.
precepts.point: The word was sent unto the children of Israel, and Peter told Cornelius, that word ye know. Remission of sins through Christ is given to his people.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
Peter told Cornelius, “To him give all the prophets witness, that through his name whosoever believeth in him shall receive remission of sins.” Isn't that what Cornelius was receiving? Joel is one of the prophets giving that witness: “And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered”.

That word whosoever again. But where is the deliverance? Not in all the heathen nations: “for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.”

The whosoever is the remnant whom the Lord shall call. Peter said to Cornelius, “That word, I say, ye know”: the Samaritans and the northern kingdom knew it, as Isaiah said Ephraim and the inhabitant of Samaria shall know, and as the woman at the well said, I know that Messias cometh. Cornelius was devout; he knew the law and that he would be called eventually. He was of that remnant.

precepts.text: Spare thy people, O Lord, wherefore should they say, Where is their God?
precepts.point: The idle in the truth will be fed Christianity. Those two years or more in the congregation must examine themselves.

note.label: Christ: the Enemy of Christianity

precepts.why:
Joel shows the same cry. “Blow the trumpet in Zion, sanctify a fast, call a solemn assembly”, and “Let the priests, the ministers of the Lord, weep between the porch and the altar, and let them say, Spare thy people, O Lord, and give not thine heritage to reproach, that the heathen should rule over them: wherefore should they say among the people, Where is their God?”

Why will we cry, Spare thy people? We just read it in Isaiah 19: because of the oppressors. They will say, we killed you, where is your God? We cut your throat, we ended your bank account, where is your God?

“Then will the Lord be jealous for his land, and pity his people.” He pities his people because we are not in the land. But he promises not to leave us alone: “Behold, I will send you corn, and wine, and oil”, “and I will no more make you a reproach among the heathen”.

“But I will remove far off from you the northern army”. That is the name the Bible gives to the power that is going to be on us: the oppressors of Isaiah 19, the great multitude of 2 Esdras 16, is the northern army. He will drive him into a land barren and desolate, with his face toward the east sea, the Dead Sea, and his hinder part toward the utmost sea, the Mediterranean, “and his stink shall come up”. The white man shall meet death when he goes to that land, because he has done evil things.

precepts.text: Ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: Respect unto His chosen is not respect of persons. Within Israel there is no respect of persons: the Most High renders to every man according to his deeds, tribulation and anguish upon every soul that doeth evil, of the Jew first and also of the Gentile, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom that was Hellenized; but glory, honour, and peace to every man that worketh good. The nation is chosen above the nations, and all Israel shall be saved through the Deliverer out of Sion.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
“And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” The Most High has respect unto one nation, Israel: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

He is in the midst of Israel, He is the Lord their God and none else, and His people shall never be ashamed. That is the respect God had unto the children of Israel when their cry came up unto him, and Israel cries in this captivity today.

precepts.text: I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Lord your God, and none else; everyone else is excluded, and my people shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: He brought them forth out of the land of Egypt that He may dwell among them: I am the Lord their God. Israel should walk confident, special, and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else; repent from spiritual fornication and return to the Most High.

note.label: Exodus 29: The Consecration of Aaron and His Sons

precepts.why:
“I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God.” Joel says the same: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

He was in no other nation's tabernacle, temple or synagogue. There is no tabernacle today, but it is still the same case: He is in the midst of Israel and none else, which excludes everybody else from the benefits of having the Most High as their God.

There is nothing to be ashamed of in the fact that He chose Israel only; “my people shall never be ashamed.” Israel should walk confident, special and chosen above all nations of people, for the Most High is faithful and belongs to no one else.

precepts.text: Ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and my people shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
Verse 14 explains why the camp had to be clean, why even easing yourself was done outside the camp: “For the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee, and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy: that he see no unclean thing in thee, and turn away from thee.”

God says the same through Joel: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” He is in the midst of Israel, and none else. Because he walks in the midst of the camp, the camp was to be holy, for we are holy, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in it.

That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle.

precepts.text: They shall run like mighty men and climb the wall like men of war; the LORD shall utter his voice before his army; Israel made into warriors once again.
precepts.point: When Christ returns he will destroy all nations in the valley of Megiddo, and after Israel's spirits are changed he will thrust out the enemy from before us and say, Destroy them. Israel will lay the vengeance of the Most High upon Edom according to his anger and according to his fury. Brothers, you just have to endure to the end; this is how you read the Bible, precept upon precept, here a little and there a little.

note.label: Joshua 11: The Northern Kings Utterly Destroyed

precepts.why:
We see the Most High setting it up right before our eyes: Israel is being made into warriors once again, so the days of Joshua can be once again when the Lord returns. “They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks: Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded.”

“The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining: And the Lord shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?” The Lord shall utter his voice before his army, as he hardened the hearts of the kings so that they came against Israel in battle and were destroyed utterly. He is setting us in order before our enemies' eyes.

precepts.text: Rend your heart, and not your garments; the Most High looks for true repentance within.
precepts.point: David asked the man how he was not afraid to stretch forth his hand to destroy the Lord's anointed. Even a man about to die was not to be touched; the judgment of the Lord was to be let play out. David then commanded one of his young men to fall upon the Amalekite, and he died, for his own mouth had testified against him.

note.label: 2 Samuel 1: David Laments Saul and Jonathan

precepts.why:
“And rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the Lord your God: for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repenteth him of the evil.”

When the news came, “David took hold on his clothes, and rent them; and likewise all the men that were with him”, and they mourned, wept and fasted until even for Saul, for Jonathan, “and for the house of Israel; because they were fallen by the sword.” The renting of garments was the sign of mourning.

But the Most High looks for a rent heart and not rent garments only. True repentance is inward, not just an outward show, and it is the heart turned unto the Lord that he is looking for.

precepts.text: They shall run like mighty men and climb the wall like men of war, every one marching in his ways without breaking ranks.
precepts.point: This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us; we just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

note.label: 2 Samuel 10: The Children of Ammon and the Syrians Smitten

precepts.why:
“They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks:”

That is Joab at the gate of Ammon. With the children of Ammon in array at the entering in of the gate and the Syrians by themselves in the field, “the front of the battle was against him before and behind”. So he chose of all the choice men of Israel against the Syrians and gave the rest into the hand of Abishai his brother against Ammon: “If the Syrians be too strong for me, then thou shalt help me: but if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee, then I will come and help thee.”

This is how much of a warrior nation Israel is: Joab put his troops in a battle array to fight two enemies at one time. That warrior mentality is already etched inside us. We just have to keep the commandments so it can come back out, as it is going to according to Joel 2.

precepts.text: Israel shall know the Most High is in their midst, their God and none else, and shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: No other nation has this. The Most High promised Israel that in a drought, if they repented and returned to Him, He would honor their prayers and send rain in due season.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 6: Solomon's Prayer of Dedication

precepts.why:
“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

No other nation has this. When the heaven is shut up and there is no rain because Israel sinned, if they pray toward this place, confess his name and turn from their sin, the Most High promised to hear, forgive, teach them the good way wherein they should walk, and “send rain upon thy land, which thou hast given unto thy people for an inheritance.”

When he answers that repentance and sends the rain in due season, Israel knows he is in their midst, their God and none else, and they are not ashamed.

precepts.text: You shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Most High your God and none else.
precepts.point: His rulership, his throne, will dwell in the midst of the children of Israel forever. He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why: “This is my rest for ever: here will I dwell; for I have desired it.” Here he will dwell in the midst of Israel: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” He is the Most High our God and none else, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

precepts.text: The Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else, and his people shall never be ashamed.
precepts.point: When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God; other heathen rulers came to the same acknowledgement, such as Antiochus and Naaman the Syrian.

note.label: Daniel 3: The Fiery Furnace and the Servants of the Most High

precepts.why:
“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” The Most High is in the midst of Israel and none else; he is our God, the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, and they were not ashamed for trusting him. They “yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own God”, and he sent his angel and delivered them.

Nebuchadnezzar understood at that time that we had our own God. He made a decree that any people, nation, or language which spake amiss against their God would be cut in pieces and their houses made a dunghill, “because there is no other God that can deliver after this sort.” Why do people not understand that today? A heathen king in Babylon saw it and said it, and yet our people today do not know that Israel has its own God.

When the nations get jacked up they come to know who has the real, true, living God. Nebuchadnezzar is not the only one: Antiochus came to the same acknowledgement, and so did Naaman the Syrian. What the heathen kings had to learn by force, Joel says Israel shall know: the Lord is in the midst of Israel, and none else, and his people shall never be ashamed.

precepts.text: The Lord is in the midst of Israel and there is none else.
precepts.point: He will not execute the fierceness of his anger, for he is God and not man, the Holy One in the midst of thee.

note.label: Hosea 11: When Israel Was a Child

precepts.why:
The Most High asks “How shall I give thee up, Ephraim? how shall I deliver thee, Israel?” His heart is turned within him, his repentings are kindled together, and he will not execute the fierceness of his anger, “for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee”.

Joel says the same of him: “ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” The Lord is in the midst of Israel and there is none else. That is why he does not return to destroy Ephraim: he is God and not man, the Holy One in the midst of his people.

precepts.text: I am in the midst of Israel and none else; I will pour out my Spirit, and whosoever shall call on the name of the Most High in Zion and Jerusalem shall be delivered.
precepts.point: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be saved" is defined by its audience. It is not the universal whosoever the churches pull from John 3:16; the whosoever is the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Peter says this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel, so go to Joel and read what comes right before the pouring out: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.” The Most High is in the midst of Israel. Then: “I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy”. All flesh is the house of Israel, not all nations, and the very next thing Peter says in Acts 2 confirms it: ye men of Israel.

The sons and daughters prophesying means they are given the ability to read and interpret the scriptures. The wonders, the blood and fire and the sun turned into darkness, are the signs before the great and terrible day of the Lord.

Then the whosoever: “whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” The whosoever is defined by its audience. Deliverance is in Zion and Jerusalem and in the remnant the Lord calls: the Israelites scattered in the different lands.

precepts.text: I am in the midst of Israel, and I am the Most High and none else, and my people shall never be ashamed, showing he is not the God of any other nation.
precepts.point: Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Not ashamed comes from Joel: “And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

He is in the midst of Israel and none else; he is not the God of any other nation. So the whosoever that believes on the stone and is not ashamed is his people, Israel.

precepts.text: Whosoever shall call on the name of the Most High shall be delivered, for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, identifying the "whosoever" as Israel and Jerusalem.
precepts.point: Christ is also a sanctuary, a place of refuge and comfort from the world, from crime, hatred, and murder, and he gives our people a purpose, which is what everybody is looking for. Simeon said the child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and the "own" that received him not is the fall of the scribes, Sadducees, and chief priests.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.”

The whosoever is identified: deliverance is in mount Zion and in Jerusalem, in the remnant the Lord calls. The stone the builders rejected became the head of the corner for Israel, and whosoever of Israel believes on him shall not be ashamed.

precepts.text: The Most High is in the midst of Israel, and whosoever calls on his name shall be delivered, for in Zion and Jerusalem shall be deliverance.
precepts.point: Paul quotes Hosea and Isaiah, not Jeremiah or Ezekiel, because his subject is the northern kingdom broken before the Assyrian captivity, and his "whosoever" is whosoever of Zion, whosoever of Israel. The Most High called a people not of the Jews only but also of the "Gentiles," meaning Ephraim.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and none else: and my people shall never be ashamed.”

“And it shall come to pass, that whosoever shall call on the name of the Lord shall be delivered: for in mount Zion and in Jerusalem shall be deliverance, as the Lord hath said, and in the remnant whom the Lord shall call.” The whosoever is inside Israel: the Most High in the midst of Israel, deliverance in Zion and Jerusalem, in the remnant he calls.
